$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{61-4\text{i}}{37}=(\frac{61}{37})+(-\frac{4}{37})\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: $\frac{5-2\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}}=$
after.worked_solution:
The denominator is $1+2\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $1-2\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $1-2\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5-2\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}} & =\frac{5-2\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}}\cdot \frac{1-2\text{i}}{1-2\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{5-10\text{i}-2\text{i}+4{\text{i}}^{2}}{{1}^{2}-{2}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{5-12\text{i}+4(-1)}{1-4(-1)} \\  & =\frac{5-12\text{i}-4}{1+4} \\  & =\frac{1-12\text{i}}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\frac{1-12\text{i}}{5}=\frac{1}{5}-\frac{12}{5}\text{i}
$$

decision.explanation: Multiply by the conjugate 6-3i. The numerator is (2-5i)(6-3i)=12-36i+15i²=-3-36i, and the denominator is 36+9=45. Dividing gives -1/15-(4/5)i, option b.

after.worked_solution:
First, we set up the fraction:

$$
\frac{2-5\text{i}}{6+3\text{i}}
$$

The denominator is $6+3\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $6-3\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $6-3\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{{z}_{1}}{{z}_{2}} & =\frac{2-5\text{i}}{6+3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{2-5\text{i}}{6+3\text{i}}\cdot \frac{6-3\text{i}}{6-3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{12-6\text{i}-30\text{i}+15{\text{i}}^{2}}{{6}^{2}-{3}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{12-36\text{i}+15(-1)}{{6}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{12-36\text{i}-15}{36+9} \\  & =\frac{-3-36\text{i}}{45}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-3-36\text{i}}{45}=-\frac{3}{45}-\frac{36}{45}\text{i}=-\frac{1}{15}-\frac{4}{5}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

The denominator is $-3+2\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $-3-2\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-3-2\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$

$$

content.problem: $\frac{6-4\text{i}}{3\text{i}}=$
content.worked_solution:
Here, the denominator is the imaginary number $3\text{i}.$ Note that this can be written as $0+3\text{i},$ so the conjugate is $0-3\text{i},$ or simply $-3\text{i}.$

So, we multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-3\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6-4\text{i}}{3\text{i}} & =\frac{6-4\text{i}}{3\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-3\text{i}}{-3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-18\text{i}+12{\text{i}}^{2}}{-9{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-18\text{i}+12(-1)}{-9(-1)} \\  & =\frac{-12-18\text{i}}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-12-18\text{i}}{9} & =-\frac{12}{9}-\frac{18}{9}\text{i} \\  & =-\frac{4}{3}-2\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
